mainTopic: Why a robber who swore must personally return the money (רבא), and whether an agent appointed in front of witnesses counts as the owner's agent
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge: if the robber admitted on his own, why does the משנה say only a robber who swore must bring the money to the owner? רבא answers that when the robber knows whom he robbed and admitted it, the owner is treated as saying 'keep it for me,' so the money becomes a פקדון. A robber who swore falsely still needs כפרה, and he gets it only when the money reaches the owner's hand. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה's rule that the robber may not pay the victim's son or agent. רב חסדא says an agent appointed in front of עדים is a real agent, and רבה says he is not. Two משניות are brought against רב חסדא, and he answers that 'his agent' there means a hired worker who was never appointed with עדים. The גמרא explains that the משנה names a court agent because that rule has no exceptions, and notes that this disagrees with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר also hold that a witnessed agent counts, and they explain our משנה in two ways. The amud ends as רב יהודה begins a new teaching in the name of שמואל.

steps.title: Closing words of the challenge: he already admitted on his own
steps.stepSummary: The challenge ends: the robber already admitted by himself, so according to רבי טרפון he should have to chase the owner even without a false oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: …since he already admitted it by himself!
steps.whatsHappening: This line is the end of a challenge that started just before this section. The גמרא is pointing out that the robber already confessed by himself, so the משנה's focus on a robber who swore looks hard to explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה implies that only a robber who swore falsely must bring the money to the owner, even far away. But a robber who confessed on his own is already a sincere בעל תשובה, and רבי טרפון holds such a person must go to any length to return the stolen money. So why does the משנה limit the rule to a case of an oath?

keyTerms.meaning: from his own mouth, without being forced or proven

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this line as a full new statement. It is only the closing words of a question that began earlier on the דף.

phrases.english: since he already admitted on his own!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a challenge that began before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from the משנה that only a robber who swore must chase the owner, if the משנה follows רבי טרפון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A robber who confessed on his own already shows real תשובה, so under רבי טרפון he should have to chase the owner even without an oath. That makes the oath detail seem unnecessary.

steps.title: רבא: the owner is treated as if he said 'keep it for me'
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the משנה is a special case. Since the robber knows the owner and admitted to him, the owner is viewed as leaving the money with the robber as a deposit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Our משנה is different. The robber knows whom he robbed and admitted it to him, and the money can be given back to its owner. So it is as if the owner told him, 'Let my money stay with you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new answer that explains why the משנה's case is special. Here the owner is known and the robber admitted to him, so the owner is considered to have left the money with the robber.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier cases were about a robber who did not know whom he robbed. In our משנה the victim is known, he heard the confession, and he could take his money back at any time. Since he did not take it, we see him as saying 'hold it for me,' which turns the stolen money into a פקדון.

keyTerms.meaning: to return the money to its owner
'let it stay with you for me' (a statement that turns the money into a deposit)

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Our mishna is different,
for since he knows whom he robbed,
and he admitted to him;
since it is possible to return the money to its owner,
it is as if he (the owner) said to him:
"Let it be kept for me in your hand."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1 by showing that the משנה's case is unusual.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (שאני): a known victim who heard the confession is treated as leaving the money as a deposit.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A robber who confessed should have to chase the owner whether or not he swore.
steps.terutzMaskana: A known owner who heard the confession is viewed as saying 'keep it for me,' so the money becomes a פקדון with the robber.

steps.title: Why the oath makes the difference
steps.stepSummary: A robber who swore falsely needs כפרה, so the deposit idea is not enough and the money must reach the owner. Without an oath, the money stays with the robber as a deposit until the owner comes for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: So if he swore, even though the owner is seen as saying 'keep it for me,' he needs atonement, and that is only complete once the money reaches the owner's hand. But if he did not swear, the money is a deposit with him until the owner comes and takes it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא applies his idea to show why the משנה mentions an oath. The oath creates a need for כפרה, and that need is what forces the robber to deliver the money himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'keep it for me' idea makes the money a deposit, and that is enough for a robber who did not swear. A robber who swore falsely must also bring a קרבן אשם, and his כפרה depends on the money actually reaching the owner. This is why the משנה's rule fits the oath case only, and the challenge from step 1 is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: a deposit (an item held for its owner)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, a known owner who heard the confession is seen as leaving the money as a deposit. That is enough when there was no oath, but a robber who swore falsely needs כפרה, and he gets it only when the money actually reaches the owner.

phrases.english: Therefore, if he swore,
even though he (the owner) is considered as saying to him:
"Let it be kept for me in your hand,"
since he needs atonement,
it is not enough until it reaches his (the owner's) hand;
but if he did not swear,
it is a deposit with him,
until he (the owner) comes and takes it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבא's principle from step 2 to the two cases, with an oath and without one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying the principle: the need for כפרה overrides the deposit idea.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the owner is seen as saying 'keep it for me,' even a robber who swore could just hold the money.
steps.terutzMaskana: A robber who swore must deliver the money to the owner for his כפרה. A robber who did not swear may hold it as a deposit.

steps.title: The משנה's 'not to his son or agent' and the dispute about an agent appointed in front of witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that the robber may not give the payment to the owner's son or agent. It then brings a dispute: רב חסדא says an agent appointed in front of witnesses is a real agent, and רבה says he is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: he should not give it to the owner's son or to his agent. It was said about an agent appointed in front of witnesses: רב חסדא said he is an agent, and רבה said he is not an agent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It brings a disagreement about an agent who was appointed in front of witnesses to collect money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says handing the money to the owner's agent does not free the robber. The question is whether appointing the agent in front of witnesses makes him a real agent. If he is, the payer is free once he hands over the money. רב חסדא says yes and רבה says no.
steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute decides who carries the risk if money is lost on its way through an agent: the payer or the owner.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִתֵּן לֹא לִבְנוֹ וְלֹא לִשְׁלוּחוֹ.
phrases.english: He may not give it to his son or to his agent.
phrases.notes: This is a quote of the next line of the משנה, about the robbery victim's son or agent.

phrases.english: It was stated: an agent whom he appointed with witnesses,
Rav Ḥisda said: he is an agent,
Rabba said: he is not an agent.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יִתֵּן לֹא לִבְנוֹ וְלֹא לִשְׁלוּחוֹ. אִיתְּמַר: שָׁלִיחַ שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ בְּעֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חסדא: an agent appointed in front of witnesses is a real agent. רבה: he is not.

steps.title: רב חסדא's reason: the witnesses were there to give the agent authority
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא reasons that the owner went to the trouble of bringing witnesses so that the money would be in the agent's control.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said he is an agent: that is exactly why the owner bothered to appoint him in front of witnesses, so that the money would come under the agent's control.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רב חסדא's view. Appointing the agent in front of witnesses shows a real, formal appointment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would the owner bother bringing witnesses? רב חסדא says it was to give the agent full authority. Once the money reaches the agent, it counts as if it reached the owner, so the payer is free.

keyTerms.meaning: in his domain / under his control

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said he is an agent,
because for this reason he took the trouble and appointed him with witnesses,
so that it would stand in his (the agent's) domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר הָוֵי שָׁלִיחַ – לְהָכִי טְרַחִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of the first side of the dispute in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The witnesses show that the owner meant to give the agent full authority, so paying the agent counts as paying the owner.

steps.title: רבה's reason: the witnesses only show the agent can be trusted
steps.stepSummary: רבה reasons that the owner only meant to say the man is trustworthy. The payer may send the money through him if he wants, but he does so at his own risk.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said he is not an agent: the owner is really saying, 'This man is trustworthy. If you want to rely on him, rely on him. If you want to send the money with him, send it with him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבה's reasoning. He reads the appointment as a recommendation, not as full agency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה says the witnesses only show that the owner trusts this man. The owner gives the payer the option of using him but does not take on the risk. So if the money is lost before it reaches the owner, the payer is still responsible.
steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא holds that an agent appointed in front of witnesses is a real agent, so payment to him frees the payer. רבה holds the owner only vouched for his honesty, so the payer still carries the risk until the money reaches the owner.

phrases.english: Rabba said he is not an agent,
this is what he (the owner) is saying: he is a trustworthy person;
if you rely on him, rely on him,
if you want to send it in his hand,
send it in his hand.
phrases.notes: The choice is yours, so if it gets lost on the way, you are the one who loses.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה אָמַר לָא הָוֵי שָׁלִיחַ – הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second side of the dispute, in contrast to רב חסדא's reasoning in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The appointment only vouches for the agent's honesty. Using him is the payer's choice, and the payer stays responsible until the money reaches the owner.

steps.title: Quoting the borrowed-cow משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: if a cow is sent to the borrower through the owner's or the borrower's son, slave, or שליח, and it dies on the way, the borrower is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: Someone borrows a cow. The owner sends it with his own son, slave, or agent, or with the borrower's son, slave, or agent. If the cow dies, the borrower is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to רב חסדא. It quotes a משנה about a borrowed cow so that it can look closely at the words 'the borrower's agent' in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A borrower is responsible for a borrowed animal only once it reaches him. The משנה says that if the cow dies while it is with the borrower's שליח, the borrower is still פטור. That suggests the שליח's hands do not count as the borrower's own hands.

phrases.english: We learned: one who borrows the cow,
phrases.notes: This משנה is in בבא מציעא, not our פרק.

phrases.english: and [the owner] sent it with his son,
with his slave, with his agent;
or with the son, with the slave,
with the agent of the borrower;
and it died — he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside משנה to test רב חסדא's view from steps 4-5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's view that a שליח appointed in front of עדים is a real agent
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only. The משנה exempts the borrower even when the cow was with his שליח.

steps.title: The borrower's agent must have had witnesses, so this contradicts רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of שליח the משנה means. If there were no עדים, how would we know he was a שליח? So there must have been עדים, and yet the borrower is פטור. That is a problem for רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This agent, what is the case? If he was not appointed in front of witnesses, how do we know he is an agent? Rather, he was appointed in front of witnesses, and the משנה still says the borrower is exempt? This is difficult for רב חסדא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the שליח in the משנה must have been appointed in front of עדים. Then it uses the ruling of פטור to attack רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב חסדא, a שליח appointed with עדים is a real agent. If so, once the cow reached him, it should count as reaching the borrower, and the borrower should be responsible. The משנה says he is פטור, which sounds like רבה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? (how do we picture it)

phrases.english: This agent, what is the case?
If he did not appoint him in front of witnesses,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording, 'appointed him.'

phrases.english: how do we know [he is an agent]?
Rather, he appointed him in front of witnesses —
and it teaches that he is exempt?
This is difficult for רב חסדא!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the משנה quoted in step 7 to attack רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that a שליח appointed with עדים is a real agent
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known שליח must have been appointed with עדים. Yet the borrower is פטור, so the cow in the שליח's hands did not count as being in the borrower's hands.

steps.title: The משנה means a hired worker
steps.stepSummary: The answer uses something רב חסדא said elsewhere: 'his agent' means his hired worker, who is known to work for him without any formal appointment in front of עדים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב חסדא said: it is talking about his hired worker or his regular harvester. Here too, it is talking about his hired worker or his regular harvester.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says the 'agent' in the משנה is a worker everyone knows serves the borrower, not someone appointed with עדים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed there are only two choices: an appointment with עדים, or no way of knowing he is an agent. There is a third choice. A hired worker is known to act for his boss even without עדים, so people call him 'his agent.' Since he was not appointed with עדים, the ruling of פטור does not contradict רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: His regular harvester (a worker always in his service)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב חסדא is changing his view. He still holds that a שליח appointed with עדים is a real agent. He is only saying the משנה is not talking about that kind of שליח.

phrases.english: As רב חסדא said:
with his hired worker or his harvester,
here too, with his hired worker or his harvester.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any known שליח must have been appointed with עדים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means a hired worker who is known to serve the borrower without any appointment in front of עדים, so it says nothing against רב חסדא.

steps.title: Our own משנה seems to contradict רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא from our משנה, which says the גזלן may not give the payment to the owner's son or שליח. A known שליח must have been appointed with עדים, so it seems even such a שליח does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: he may not give it to his son or to his agent. This agent, what is the case? If he did not appoint him in front of witnesses, how do we know? Rather, is it not that he appointed him in front of witnesses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes the same kind of attack, but this time from our own משנה about returning stolen money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a שליח appointed with עדים is a real agent, as רב חסדא says, then the גזלן should be able to pay him and be done. Our משנה says he may not. That sounds like רבה's view.

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: לֹא יִתֵּן לֹא לִבְנוֹ וְלֹא לִשְׁלוּחוֹ.
phrases.english: We learned: He may not give it to his son nor to his agent.
phrases.notes: This is our own משנה, already quoted in step 4.

phrases.english: This agent, what is the case?
If he did not appoint him in front of witnesses,
how do we know?
Rather, is it not that he appointed him in front of witnesses?

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: לֹא יִתֵּן לֹא לִבְנוֹ וְלֹא לִשְׁלוּחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רב חסדא, built the same way as step 8 but taken from our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that a שליח appointed with עדים is a real agent
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known שליח must have been appointed with עדים. Yet paying him does not count as returning the money, which goes against רב חסדא.

steps.title: Again, a hired worker
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that our משנה, too, means the owner's hired worker, who was never appointed with עדים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא explained it as talking about his hired worker or his regular harvester.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the second challenge the same way as the first: the 'agent' in the משנה is just a known worker of the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the hired worker was never appointed in front of עדים, he is not a real agent even according to רב חסדא. So the גזלן cannot fulfill his duty by paying him. A שליח appointed with עדים would be a different case.
steps.whatToRemember: Both משניות that say 'his agent' does not count are explained by רב חסדא as talking about a hired worker who was never appointed with עדים. His view stands: a שליח appointed in front of עדים is a real agent.

phrases.english: רב חסדא explained it:
with his hired worker or his harvester.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10 the same way as step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שליח in our משנה was appointed in front of עדים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שליח in our משנה is a hired worker with no appointment in front of עדים, so paying him does not count, even according to רב חסדא.

steps.title: Why didn't the משנה mention an agent appointed with witnesses?
steps.stepSummary: If an agent appointed with עדים is a real agent, the משנה should have said so instead of switching to a court agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about an agent the victim appointed in front of witnesses? Is he really a valid agent? If so, instead of the last part of the משנה saying 'but he may give it to a court agent,' it should have made the distinction within the same case: 'an agent appointed in front of witnesses is a valid agent!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that an agent appointed with עדים counts. If he did, the משנה would have mentioned him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said the משנה's 'שליח' is only a hired worker who was never appointed with עדים. That suggests an agent appointed with עדים would count. But then the משנה's next clause should have said 'an agent with עדים is fine' instead of jumping to a totally different kind of agent, a שליח בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: whom he appointed in front of witnesses
the last part of a משנה
let it make the distinction within the same case

phrases.english: But an agent whom he appointed in front of witnesses — what is the law?
Is he indeed a valid agent?
Instead of teaching in the last part:

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נוֹתֵן הוּא לִשְׁלִיחַ בֵּית דִּין;
phrases.english: "But he may give it to an agent of the court,"
let it make the distinction in the same case and teach:
phrases.notes: He means: stay with the victim's own agent and just add the case of one appointed with עדים.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁלִיחַ שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ בְּעֵדִים, הָכִי נָמֵי דְּהָוֵי שָׁלִיחַ!
phrases.english: an agent appointed in front of witnesses is indeed a valid agent!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל שָׁלִיחַ שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ בְּעֵדִים – מַאי, הָכִי נָמֵי דְּהָוֵי שָׁלִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what follows from step 11: if only an unwitnessed agent fails, the witnessed agent should have been mentioned.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that an agent appointed with עדים is a valid agent for returning stolen property.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's choice of wording: it lists only a court agent as acceptable, which suggests a witnessed agent is not.

steps.title: The משנה chose the rule that has no exceptions
steps.stepSummary: A court agent works no matter who appointed him; a witnessed agent works only if the victim appointed him, so the משנה picked the clean rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: the rule about a witnessed agent was not clear-cut. A court agent counts whether the victim or the robber asked for him, so that rule is clear-cut. But a witnessed agent counts only if the victim appointed him, not if the robber did, so it is not clear-cut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה preferred to teach a rule that works in every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A witnessed agent really does count, but only when the נגזל appointed him; a גזלן cannot appoint someone to receive the payment for the victim. A שליח בית דין is valid no matter which side asked for him. A משנה likes to state a rule without exceptions, so it mentioned the court agent.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not clear-cut for him (the rule has exceptions)

steps.whatToRemember: An agent appointed with עדים is valid only if the victim appointed him. A court agent is valid no matter who asked for him. That is why the משנה mentions only the court agent.

phrases.english: They say: it was not a clear-cut rule for him;
an agent of the court,
no difference whether the victim appointed him
and no difference whether the robber appointed him,
he is an agent — that is clear-cut for him.
But an agent appointed in front of witnesses,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי עֲשָׂאוֹ נִגְזָל הוּא דְּהָוֵי שָׁלִיחַ,
phrases.english: where only when the victim appointed him is he an agent,
but if the robber appointed him he is not an agent —
that is not clear-cut for him.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the משנה's choice of wording: it teaches only rules with no exceptions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leaving out the witnessed agent means he does not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: A witnessed agent does count when the victim appointed him; he was left out only because that rule depends on who appointed him.

steps.title: Our משנה disagrees with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The rule that a court agent counts even when the robber asked for him rejects רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: This rejects the view of this תנא, as it was taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: a court agent whom the victim appointed and not the robber, or whom the robber appointed and then the victim sent for and took his item from him, the robber is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the rule 'a court agent counts no matter who asked for him' disagrees with another תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds that a court agent set up at the robber's request frees the robber only once the victim actually takes the item from the agent. Our משנה holds that handing it to any court agent frees the robber right away.

keyTerms.meaning: and this comes to exclude (reject) a view
a sage of the משנה period

phrases.english: And this excludes the view of this תנא —

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as it was taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says:
a court agent whom the victim appointed
and the robber did not appoint,
or the robber appointed him

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁלַח הַלָּה וְנָטַל אֶת שֶׁלּוֹ מִיָּדוֹ –
phrases.english: and the other one sent and took his item from his hand —
phrases.notes: 'The other one' is the victim, taking his item from the agent.

phrases.english: he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a side comment: the rule stated in step 13 about court agents goes against a known תנא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Our משנה frees the robber as soon as he gives the item to any court agent, against רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who requires the victim to take it when the robber was the one who asked for the agent.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר: a witnessed agent counts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר both rule that an agent appointed with עדים is a valid agent, and they begin to deal with our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר both say: an agent appointed in front of witnesses is a valid agent. And if you will say: what about our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים state that an agent appointed with עדים counts. Then the גמרא sets up the next move: an expected objection from our משנה, which is answered right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This agrees with רב חסדא's approach from the earlier steps. The phrase 'and if you will say: our משנה' brings up the problem that our משנה seems to reject the victim's agent, and the answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you will say (bringing up an expected objection)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר both say:
An agent appointed in front of witnesses is a valid agent.
And if you will say: our משנה —

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the main question of the witnessed agent and brings support from two אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An agent appointed with עדים is a valid agent.

steps.title: The משנה is about a victim who only casually supplied a messenger
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר explain that the משנה's agent is someone the victim merely sent to remind the robber, with no formal appointment.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is talking about a case where the victim supplies the robber with a messenger. He says to someone: 'I have money with so-and-so, and he isn't sending it. Go show yourself to him. Maybe he just can't find anyone to send it with.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר answer the problem from our משנה. The agent there was never really appointed. The victim just casually sent someone over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They hold that an agent appointed with עדים is a real agent, yet the משנה says the robber is still liable if he gives the money to an agent. Their answer is that the משנה's agent was only told 'go show yourself to him.' That is a reminder, not a real שליחות, so the victim never took on the risk.

keyTerms.meaning: He supplies him with a messenger: makes someone available, without a formal appointment
Show yourself to him, let him see you

steps.confusionAlert: This messenger is not an agent appointed with עדים. The victim never said 'take the money for me.' He only sent someone to remind the robber, so the robber who hands it over is still responsible.

phrases.english: Where he provides him with an agent,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the robbery victim, and 'him' is the robber.

phrases.english: in that he says to him:
'I have money with so-and-so,
and he is not sending it.
Present yourself to him,

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא אִינִישׁ הוּא דְּלָא מַשְׁכַּח לְשַׁדּוֹרֵי לֵיהּ״.
phrases.english: perhaps he is a person who cannot find someone to send it with.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer that רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר began in Step 15 to reconcile their view with the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seems to say that any agent, even one appointed with עדים, does not free the robber from liability.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only means a messenger the victim casually sent without real appointment. An agent appointed with עדים does free the robber.

steps.title: A second answer, like רב חסדא: the victim's hired worker
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the משנה is talking about the victim's hired worker or harvester, as רב חסדא said.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else, it is like רב חסדא said: the משנה is talking about the victim's hired worker or his harvester.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way for רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר to explain the משנה. They borrow רב חסדא's answer from earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in Step 11, רב חסדא said the משנה means the owner's worker, who was never appointed with עדים. Here that same answer works for רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר. The worker is connected to the victim but was never made his agent for this money, so the robber who gives it to him stays liable.

keyTerms.meaning: His harvester, a regular worker who gathers his crops

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר hold that an agent appointed with עדים is a real agent. They read the משנה as talking about someone who was never truly appointed: either a messenger the victim casually sent, or the victim's worker.

phrases.english: Alternatively, it is in accordance with רב חסדא –
phrases.notes: This is רב חסדא's answer from earlier in the סוגיא.

phrases.english: with regard to his hired hand or his harvester.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, alternative answer alongside Step 16, reusing רב חסדא's answer from Step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seems to rule out even a properly appointed agent.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about the victim's worker, who was never appointed with עדים, so the view of רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר stands.

steps.title: Opening a new statement from רב יהודה in the name of שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a new teaching about appointing agents, said by רב יהודה in the name of שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is only a setup. The גמרא is about to bring a new statement from שמואל, and the statement itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion of the משנה's agent is finished, and a new topic about appointing agents begins. For now we only know who is speaking. The actual rule follows right after.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says that Shmuel says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on appointing agents after the reconciliation of the משנה is complete.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduction only. שמואל's actual ruling follows in the next part of the text.
